# tmux

[tmux.github.io](https://tmux.github.io) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/tmux](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/tmux)

**Status: available.** 4 of OSS-Fuzz's 6 fuzz targets have statements. 16 binaries, 42 MB. 28 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 28 blocked by the model, 0 open.

Built from tmux (commit `f763f945`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [cmd-parse-fuzzer](cmd-parse-fuzzer/) | cmd_parse_from_buffer on the input (<=2048 bytes) with CMD_PARSE_QUIET; the command list or error is freed. Parse status is only used to pick what to free. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |
| [format-fuzzer](format-fuzzer/) | format_expand on the NUL-terminated input with eight fixed format variables; the expansion is freed unread. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |
| [input-fuzzer](input-fuzzer/) | input_parse_buffer feeds the input (<=512 bytes) to an 80x25 pane's terminal-escape parser, then drains the command queue and runs the libevent loop once. | 1 check (invariant; all confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 blocked by the model |
| [style-fuzzer](style-fuzzer/) | style_parse on the NUL-terminated input (<=512 bytes) into a zeroed style/grid_cell; the return code and result are ignored. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |

Not included: **json-fuzzer** (not built yet); **layout-fuzzer** (not built yet).

## What the statements say, for tmux
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

The harnesses with a check whose failure ends the process with a status that a halts statement excludes, so that a proof of that statement implies the check on every input it covers:
- `input-fuzzer`: after parsing the input and draining queued commands, the window's reference count is exactly 1 (only the harness's own reference), i.e. input processing leaked no window reference and did not drop one.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch tmux
    ./oft verify-sha tmux

By hand: download `tmux-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/tmux/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [tmux/tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) at `f763f94556fbd68685c02d6eea306c1a6982270e`, built with autotools
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
